# Creator Foundation (TEST FIXTURE)

> [!warning] Synthetic test data
> This is a fictional creator ("Sam Rivera") used only to run the vid-* eval
> harness. It is not Billy's real foundation. Frozen on purpose so evals are
> reproducible. Do not edit casually: changing it can invalidate fixtures (see
> tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.md).

## Iceberg statement

You do not have a time problem, you have a systems problem. The work that feels
like it has to be you almost never does. You can build the system once and the
business stops depending on you being in the room. Most service owners try to
fix overwhelm by working more hours. That makes the business heavier, not
bigger. The real move is to take the work out of your head and put it into a
system someone else can run.

## Avatar

Solo service business owner. Agency, consultant, or freelancer doing roughly
ten to forty thousand a month. Thirty-something to forty-something. Wears every
hat. The business runs on their personal effort and they feel it. They are
proud of being the one who can do the work, and that pride is exactly what keeps
them stuck. They are scared that hiring or documenting will lower quality, so
they keep doing it themselves and stay slammed.

## Top 3 problems (viewer language)

1. **I am drowning in the work and there is never enough time.** Every week is
   delivery, delivery, delivery, and there is no room to work on the business.
2. **Everything depends on me. I cannot delegate or step away.** If they take a
   week off, the business stops. They are the bottleneck on everything.
3. **I am undercharging and overworking and I know it.** They suspect their
   prices are too low, but raising them feels risky, so they grind instead.

## Content pillars

- **systems** (build the thing that does the work for you)
- **delegation** (get it out of your head and off your plate)
- **pricing** (charge what the outcome is worth, stop trading time for money)
- **mindset** (the identity shift from operator to owner)

## Credibility (fixture)

Built a service business, documented it, and stepped out of delivery. Has
helped service owners pull recurring work out of their heads and into systems
their teams run. Numbers in this fixture are illustrative only.
